best_for: Windows users who already live in Microsoft 365 and Copilot, and IT admins who need a Chromium browser they can roll out by MSI and keep on a slower update track.
description:
Microsoft Edge is the web browser made by Microsoft and the one that comes with Windows. It is proprietary software.

Split screen puts two websites side by side in one window, and the built-in PDF reader lets you mark up and edit PDFs without another app. With Remix, you tell Edge how a page should look or work: strip the clutter from an article, say, or turn a recipe into a shopping list. On the safety side, a scareware blocker stops fake virus warnings and pop-ups that push you to call bogus support lines, Secure Network protects your connection on public Wi-Fi, and a password generator suggests strong passwords. Microsoft notes that some features depend on your device, country and browser version.

points.title: Free, with Microsoft services built in
points.text: Edge costs nothing. Microsoft pitches Copilot working across your open tabs, shopping tools that check prices and look for coupons, Microsoft Rewards points and Bing. If you want a plain browser, expect to turn some of this off.

points.title: Tabs that go to sleep
points.text: Sleeping tabs, energy saver and startup boost are there to cut memory and battery use on laptops with many tabs open. Passwords, favorites and settings can sync between devices.

points.title: A new major version every two weeks
points.text: From version 152 the Stable channel moved to a two-week major release cycle. Managed business setups can pick Extended Stable, which moves every eight weeks instead. Home users get the fast track.

points.title: Macs need Ventura now
points.text: Edge 151 and newer require macOS 13 or later. macOS 12 stopped at Edge 150 and macOS 11 at Edge 138. The Mac download here is a universal build for Intel and Apple silicon.

points.title: Windows 10 still gets updates
points.text: Microsoft says Edge keeps updating on Windows 10 22H2 until at least October 2028, without paying for Extended Security Updates. The Windows packages listed here are machine-wide MSI installers for x64, 32-bit x86 and Arm64.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is a community wrapper
points.text: Microsoft supports 64-bit Ubuntu 18.04+, Debian 10+, openSUSE 15.5+ and Fedora 39+. The Flatpak listed here names Microsoft as developer, but Flathub does not mark it as verified, and it is x64 only.

points.title: Only Windows keeps a long history
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 197 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
